issues.description: Local `identity` and `coerceNumber` shadow the project's `accessors.identity` and silently change `toNumber`'s null semantics.
issues.detail: The original used `identity` from `accessors.js` and passed `toNumber` directly. The new file introduces a local `identity` and a `coerceNumber` that maps `toNumber(x) ?? 0`. That complects two concerns: type-shape adaptation and a behavioral substitution for null. A non-numeric domain entry that previously yielded `NaN` now becomes `0`, silently shifting pan/zoom output. Keep the value semantics; widen the type instead.

issues.description: `isNonEmpty` guard is essential, but `peek` overload already encodes the same fact and is being thrown away.
issues.detail: You added a `peek` overload that proves non-emptiness in the type system, then re-prove it at runtime with `isNonEmpty` and a thrown error. Pick one source of truth for that fact. Either narrow the parameter to `NonEmptyArray<number>` and let callers check at the edge, or keep the runtime check and drop the overload ceremony. Right now the same invariant lives in two places.

issues.description: Adding a runtime throw is a behavior change smuggled under a `refactor` label.
issues.detail: PR title says "Make transform functions typesafe," body says "same runtime behavior as before," then adds `error('Domain array must not be empty')` on a path that previously returned `[NaN, NaN]` silently. That is a semantic change, not a refactor. Name it: callers that relied on the silent NaN path will now throw. Worth a separate commit and a changelog note.

issues.description: `Anchor = number | null | undefined` complects "absent" with "explicitly null" at the type level.
issues.detail: The runtime check `anchor != null` collapses both into one case, which is fine, but the type advertises three states where the function treats two. Either narrow to `number | null` (matching the original JS contract) or `number | undefined`, and let callers pass one canonical "no anchor" value. Small thing; it's the kind of incidental option-shape that accretes.

issues.description: Domain is typed `number[]` but the functions only ever use `domain[0]` and `peek(domain)` — the value is really a pair.
issues.detail: The essential data here is two endpoints. Typing the parameter as `number[]` (or `NonEmptyArray<number>`) lets callers pass `[1,2,3,4]` and silently ignores the middle. If the contract is "first and last," say so in the type: `readonly [number, number]` or `readonly [number, ...number[], number]`. The current shape hides what the function actually consumes.

review.summary: The PR is a small, mostly mechanical JS-to-TS pass, and the `peek` overload is a clean piece of type work. The trouble is what got complected on the way: a runtime throw (real behavior change) is folded into a "refactor," and `toNumber` is silently replaced by a `coerceNumber` that turns null into zero — two concerns (shape adaptation and null handling) braided into one wrapper. The non-empty invariant is now asserted in both the type system (via `peek` overload) and at runtime (via `isNonEmpty`), which is one source of truth too many. Decompose: keep value semantics identical, pick one place to enforce non-emptiness, and call the behavior change what it is in the PR description.
